exercise.name: Resistance Band One Leg Kickback (Bent Position)

reference.title: Resistance Band One Leg Kickback (Bent Position)
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.

equipment: Resistance band (mini loop around the ankles)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the leg kicks back, inhale as it returns.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s back, 0.5 s squeeze, 1.8 s down

prescription.progression: Stronger band, or a pause at the top

cues.text: Band around the ankles; hinge forward with a flat back on a soft left knee, hands on the hips.
Breathe out and drive the right heel back and up until the leg lines up with the trunk.
Squeeze the glute; keep the hips square to the floor.
Breathe in and lower the leg slowly under the hip.
Keep the hinge and the band tension; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.fix: Keep the chest long and the back flat in the hinge.
Stop when the leg lines up with the trunk; higher only arches the low back.

mistakes.mistake: Opening the hip to the side
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones facing the floor.
Pause at the top, slow down.

kinematics.norm: From about 50 degrees of flexion to 10-20 degrees past neutral (clinical opinion); hip extension excites the gluteus maximus (Macadam 2019; Neto 2020)
About 40-50 degrees forward, flat back (clinical opinion)
Mini loop around both ankles (elastic resistance, Andersen 2010)

sources.title: GymVisual #9141, Resistance Band One Leg Kickback (Bent Position), video (movement reference)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Krause Neto, Soares, Vieira et al. 2020, gluteus maximus activation during common strength and hypertrophy exercises: a systematic review (J Sports Sci Med 19(1):195-203)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjørnlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Check the band for nicks before use.
modify: Poor balance: hold a support in front.
Low-back discomfort: hinge less and shorten the range.
regressions: Resistance band leg kickback (upright, hands on a wall).

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hip against the band; the hinged trunk lets the hip work through more range (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hold the hinge on the stance leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Stops the low back arching (clinical opinion).
